Jungle graphic: plays up a ride-to-paradise theme, sharing the board's eclectic personality through the depth and color of the jungle landscape 112. The Jungle graphic was created using AI — it is the only board in Burton's 2025-2026 line designed this way 113. The AI-generated graphic caused online outrage, disappointment, and frustration among the snowboarding community 114. Glow colourway: Neon-inspired, glow-in-the-dark ink highlights the Channel and base lettering 115. What is new on the 2026 model: Graphics (no construction changes) 116. The Burton Custom Camber feels on the light side of medium, bordering on being pretty lightweight 117. Exact weight not published because with wood cores, there is no consistency in a board's weight 118. OutdoorShell.com review score: 87/100, positioned solidly among the best aggressive all-mountain boards 119. Board of the World review score: 89.52/100 (4.5/5) 120. Board of the World ranking: 9th out of 38 boards in the all mountain category 121. Board of the World ranking: 8th out of 36 boards reviewed in the park category 122. Snowboarding Profiles top all-mountain boards ranking: #4, described as a board you can get more aggressive on but has enough forgiveness to be chill 123. The Ski Monster customer review: "The build quality is top-tier... The Jungle graphic looks even better in person, and the board feels durable and well-crafted. 10/10" 124. Camber measurement: 11mm of camber measured on the 156cm (SnowboardingProfiles review) 125. Edge hold: Impressed with edge-hold on both icy groomers and hard-packed snow; traditional camber profile delivers powerful turns that feel stable and precise 126. Carving: For medium to moderately high speeds, the Custom was "just so fun to carve" — full camber profile no doubt helping 127. Pop: Struck a perfect balance of being easy enough to access but with really good total pop after winding it up 128. Speed stability: The board feels stable at top speeds and the sintered base allows for smooth gliding over varying snow conditions without losing momentum 129. Landing: "I could really stomp landings on this board... if you got it a bit wrong, it was still quite forgiving of errors" 130. Catchiness: Less catchy than expected for full camber — "I hardly noticed any catchiness, unless I was trying to feel it" 131. Confidence: "This is the type of board that feels so intuitive and precise that it makes you more confident to go bigger, faster, and try new tricks" 132. Dampness: The carbon and glass work together to create a dampness that absorbs the noise other boards tend to feel 133. Tree riding: When navigating tight trees and bumpy terrain, the Custom Camber shines with its ability to react quickly to uneven terrain 134. Powder limitation: In powder, the board's mid-stiff flex and camber profile make it a bit more challenging to maneuver than other boards with rocker profiles 135. Powder performance: "not going to be awesome for powder... probably a back leg burner in deeper powder" 136. Edge hold criticism (The Good Ride): "A little behind in grip these days... on the same day, same boot, same binding, same run, the same board just doesn't grip as well as many other boards out there" 137. Buttering difficulty: The full camber makes it a little more difficult to butter compared to many boards with early rise in the tip/tail 138. Forgiveness: "This is full on camber and even though the flex is mellow/medium the consequences are not. This is for expert riders or very confident/competent advanced riders" 139. Not for: Aggressive riders who demand the stiffest board (The Ski Monster expert opinion) 140. Speed ceiling: Has limits at very high speed — "can't bomb it as fast as possible without it feeling a bit unstable, but that ceiling limit is fairly high" 141. Chunder/crud: "Not quite as damp feeling as the Custom X, but it is more damp than average" 142. Perfect for: Intermediate to advanced riders who want one all-mountain board that will perform well in all conditions 143. Top pick for intermediate to expert riders looking to take their all-mountain riding to the next level; for riders who like to charge down challenging terrain and carve through steep slopes 144. Suitable for just about every type of rider, especially those who would benefit from something that feels effortless to maneuver 145. Forum opinion: "I think the Burton Custom is a great first board to buy! I agree it is great to get started on full camber so you learn to ride with good habits" 146. comparable_board_same_brand: Also comes in Burton Custom Flying V bend (rocker/camber/rocker) for a more forgiving and versatile ride [MERCHANT] 147. The Flying V is a hybrid profile with rocker between feet and camber sections out towards nose and tail — suits beginner to intermediate riders 148. Women's equivalent: Burton Feelgood, available in 142cm, 146cm, 149cm, and 152cm sizes — practically the same board with different graphic and smaller sizes; tech is all the same 149. Wide version: Same snappy response and camber grip but with broader waists to eliminate toe/heel drag for boot sizes 11+ 150. Burton Custom X price: $899.95 at evo.com — the hardest charging board in Burton's lineup, stiffer and more aggressive 151. 30th Anniversary Custom: $679.95 at evo.com, featuring OG Pegasus-inspired graphics with modern tech 152. vs Jones Mountain Twin: The Custom Camber excels with precise carving and strong jump performance for the more experienced, mild to aggressive resort rider 153. vs Jones Mountain Twin: The Jones is often the better option for newer riders because the flex pattern and feel are more forgiving/less catchy, with easier turn initiation 154. vs Jones Mountain Twin: Jones has better edge hold for icy conditions due to Traction Tech 2.0 (additional contact points to help grip ice) 155. Price comparison vs Jones Mountain Twin: The Custom Camber is $120 more expensive than the Jones Mountain Twin 156. vs Capita DOA: If you prioritize carving, riding in light powder, going fast, go with the Custom Camber; DOA is more park/freestyle focused 157. vs Capita DOA: In head-to-head versatility, the DOA earned 9 out of 13 possible points — just one point shy of the Custom Camber 158. Capita DOA: Flex 5.5/10, true twin, hybrid camber, priced at $580 — considered exceptional value for performance 159. The Burton Custom Camber ($679.95) offers a strong balance of stability and playfulness, perfect for carving and hitting the park (Board of the World top AM list) 160. The Inertia 2026 best snowboards: The Custom is "no slouch" with "plenty of appeal for a whole range of riders" but was knocked out of top picks this year 161. Forum opinion (negative): "In the crowded all mt twin space I find the custom is an uninspired and over priced choice. It basically hasn't changed in the last 20 years" 162. Forum opinion: A snowboard shop employee said "Burton has kinda been left behind with their board tech and there are other options out there to try" 163. The Good Ride criticism: "The Burton Custom Camber is not the one-board quiver it used to be for most riders. It's missing the float and edge hold that many All-Mountain peers have" 164. resin: Super Sap Epoxy (bio-based, 50% carbon footprint reduction) [MERCHANT] [11] 165. Forestry certification: FSC certified materials, FSC-C124994 166. Sustainability: FSC-certified wood cores, Super Sap resin, and other intentional material choices incorporated into the Custom 167. Burton EST bindings are ONLY compatible with the Burton Channel system 168. All major binding brands are compatible with the Burton Channel system and 2x4 patterns 169. Recommended binding pairing: Burton Cartel EST with hinge tech for maximum pop (The Good Ride) 170. Tested pairing: Burton Cartel bindings — dialed in for aggressive riding 171. Recommended to stay below Burton's max recommended weight range because the model is light and poppy, it likes a lighter rider 173. evo.com: Major US online snowboard retailer, offers lowest price guarantee, up to 1-year returns, free shipping [11][15] 174. The Ski Monster: Founded to fill a gap in the retail experience; crew tests everything they sell, firsthand experience-based recommendations 177. Amazon: Available with Prime shipping, major retailer [35] 178. Burton.com: Manufacturer direct, full warranty support, Burton Guides available at (800) 881-3138 [9] 179.
